campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 15, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered updates to the city's theater use policy, a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for a resurfacing project, and the annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27. The council also considered a budget adjustment related to replacing remaining equipment or infrastructure.
keyTopics: Proposed modifications to Council Policy Section 14 (theater use policy), effective September 16th
Cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose, not to exceed $335,000, for a resurfacing project
Annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27
Budget adjustment to fund replacement of remaining equipment

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business including meeting minutes and vendor payments, plus land-use matters like final map approvals for two lot splits. The Council also considered two appeals of Planning Commission decisions on residential development projects and discussed law enforcement service options ahead of upcoming town hall meetings.
keyTopics: Final map approvals for lot splits at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Appeal of a single-family residence and ADU design review/setback variance approval at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of a three-lot subdivision approval (tentative map, design review, and CEQA exemption) at 14486 Oak Place
Discussion of law enforcement service options ahead of September 19 and 30 town hall meetings
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered routine business including updated city employee pay schedules, a contract increase for an electrical maintenance vendor, and changes to a volunteer awards committee. Council members also discussed renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, a citizen initiative about zoning impacts, and set up a process for the City Manager's annual performance review.
keyTopics: Resolution to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street
Contract amendment adding $250,000 to Bear Electrical Solutions' maintenance agreement
Disbanding the joint Los Altos-Los Altos Hills Volunteer Awards Committee to form a Los Altos-only committee
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning
Discussion of the Environmental Commission and possible formation of a Council subcommittee

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business at this meeting, including approval of minutes from a prior closed session and regular meeting, and a monthly financial and investment report for July 2026. The Council also considered several contract-related items, including amendments to service agreements and professional services agreements with outside vendors.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the September 1, 2026 closed session and regular Town Council meetings
Monthly Financial and Investment Report for July 2026
A second amendment to an existing agreement
A first amendment to a Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) services agreement
New professional services agreements with outside contractors

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 16, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming September 22 and September 29, 2026 City Council agendas, including whether to add items or set specific meeting times. The committee also considered several City Council-sponsored special event approvals involving city funds and donated materials, along with a proposal on self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores.
keyTopics: Review and adjustments to the September 22 and September 29, 2026 draft/final City Council agendas
Approval of free use of the Janet Gray Hayes Rotunda for a Santa Clara County Association of Realtors event in November 2026
Retroactive approval of the Santos Family Car Show as a Council District 4 sponsored special event
Retroactive approval of several Council District 5 sponsored special events
Proposal on self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — September 14, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to hear public comments, do a team-building exercise, and go over its proposed work plan for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Members also had a chance to share updates and comments before wrapping up.
keyTopics: Public oral communications period for community input
Team-building activity for committee members
Review of the Youth Advisory Committee's Fiscal Year 2026-27 work plan
Committee and staff comments, questions, and reports

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 19, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: This was a special morning session of the Sunnyvale City Council held for the annual 'State of the City' event, rather than a regular business meeting. The agenda covered event logistics and standard procedural information for the public, with no substantive policy items or votes listed.
keyTopics: Special Council meeting held for the State of the City event

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met on September 15, 2026, with closed-session discussions on potential litigation and property negotiations with the Cupertino Union School District over 10480 Finch Avenue, followed by a recognition of Cupertino High School FBLA students. The regular meeting included a large consent calendar covering meeting minutes, accounts payable, an audit committee ordinance, an AI policy, and a response to a county grand jury report on pothole damage claims, while an ordinance on building code definitions was postponed to October 6, 2026.
keyTopics: Closed session on real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of Cupertino High School students for their FBLA National Leadership Conference achievements
Postponement of an ordinance revising municipal code definitions for 'attic,' 'garages,' and 'square footage'
Adoption of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) City Council Policy and second reading of Audit Committee duties ordinance
Approval of the City's response to the Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury report on pothole damage claims

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: Santa Clara's City Council held a special meeting that began with interviews and appointments to fill two seats on the Civil Service Commission, followed by a joint meeting with the Stadium Authority Board. The Council also considered a janitorial services contract amendment, a historic preservation agreement for a property on Jackson Street, and annual workplans for various city boards and commissions.
keyTopics: Interviews and appointment of two applicants to the Civil Service Commission
Recognition of outgoing commissioners from several city boards and commissions
Contract amendment negotiations with Impec Group for citywide janitorial services
Mills Act historical preservation agreement for 1261 Jackson Street
Review and approval of FY 2026-2027 workplans for city boards, commissions, and committees

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a batch of budget and finance items, including federal housing/community development grant funding, refinancing of old redevelopment agency bonds, and an update on red light cameras. Council members also received a report on the physical condition of the Milpitas Community Center.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program presentation
Condition of the Milpitas Community Center report
Resolutions related to the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including sale and issuance of refunding bonds

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Planning & Transportation Commission — September 9, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Planning & Transportation Commission considered a proposed ordinance amending the municipal code to address City Council direction on allowing accessory dwelling units (ADUs) to be sold separately from the primary home. The Commission also received a Director's Report, discussed its meeting schedule and member assignments, and reviewed draft minutes from its August 12, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Proposed ordinance amending Municipal Code Titles 18 and 21 regarding separate sale of accessory dwelling units (ADUs)
Director's Report to the Commission
Commission meeting schedule and member assignments
Approval of draft minutes from the August 12, 2026 meeting
